openhands_r7_rolling_wal.revision: Replace the unbounded full chain journal with a fixed-size rolling WAL containing one committed-prefix candidate plus one pending event candidate, then an exact-save phase payload. Before preparing event N+1, exact-read/verify pending N and promote its candidate; crash before N+1 replays committed N, crash after N+1 replays pending N+1. This bounds marker growth to O(base snapshot size).
exact_source_reasoning: The WAL hook must be reached from ConversationState.append_event after authoritative parent stamping, but exact event JSON should come from EventLog.append after its serialization and validation and before FileStore.write. A new optional before_write callback on EventLog.append preserves fork's direct append behavior when absent.

LocalConversation callbacks run inside ConversationState contexts at emission sites, so hook-emitted nested events can participate in one deferred base save; rolling promotion is needed to recover the exact durable prefix.
Fernet makes independent base serialization byte-unstable; _save_base_state must serialize once, WAL-upgrade with those exact bytes, write the same bytes, then cleanup.

A finalized WAL left by cleanup failure can be cleaned in the same generation only when raw base exactly equals final WAL digest; if base is still old it blocks new appends. Incomplete same-generation recovery remains fail-closed.
Recovery must occur immediately after lease claim before credential scrub/LocalConversation construction. Normal takeover accepts any strictly older generation, not only G-1.
not_claimed: Python type-check or upstream pytest pass

rmcp_router_first_persistent_seam.revision: A custom task-capable call_tool is unnecessary and weaker. Keep #[tool_handler]'s generated call_tool so ToolRouter disabled-route checks and standard typed extractors run first; make the registered tool handler itself do side-effect-free MRTR preflight and persistent create-or-get on retry, then override only get_task/update_task/cancel_task/get_info.
exact_source_reasoning: tool_handler macro generates call_tool only when absent and routes ToolCallContext through ToolRouter.call.
ToolRouter.call rejects disabled tools before invocation and standard Parameters extraction occurs before handler body.
Registered tool handlers can return InputRequiredResult or CallToolResponse::Task because IntoCallToolResult supports both shapes.

RequestContext, RequestState, Parameters and Extension<T> are exact registered-tool extractors. RequestStateCodec associated_data can bind principal and intent; it supplies integrity/TTL, not single-use.
The handler itself must check client Tasks capability before create-or-get because the generic Service dispatcher task-capability guard runs only after call_tool returns.

Stock TaskManager remains concrete process-local HashMap machinery with TaskContext tied to TaskManagerInner; no released storage backend trait/create-or-get injection was found. Persistent task behavior therefore remains application-owned.
